definitions.explanation: The name of a geographical location such as a city, town, region, mountain, or river.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧{地名|ちめい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{由来|ゆらい}→由来：05451_yurai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{知|し}っていますか→知る：00458_shiru⟧。
examples.english: Do you know the origin of this place name?

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{読|よ}み→読む：00426_yomu⟧⟦にくい→〜にくい：02005_nikui⟧{地名|ちめい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: There are many place names in Japan that are difficult to read.

examples.japanese: {地名|ちめい}⟦{辞典|じてん}→辞典：01640_jiten⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{調|しら}べた→調べる：01213_shiraberu⟧。
examples.english: I looked it up in a place name dictionary.

notes:
INTERESTING FACTS:
- Many Japanese place names use unusual kanji readings (⟦{難読|なんどく}→難読：18388_nandoku⟧{地名|ちめい})
- Examples of difficult readings: {五十嵐|いがらし}, {御徒町|おかちまち}, {酒々井|しすい}

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {地名|ちめい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{由来|ゆらい}→由来：05451_yurai⟧ (origin of a place name)
- {地名|ちめい}⟦{辞典|じてん}→辞典：01640_jiten⟧ (place name dictionary)
- ⟦{難読|なんどく}→難読：18388_nandoku⟧{地名|ちめい} (place names that are hard to read)
- ⟦{珍|ちん}→珍しい：01200_mezurashii⟧{地名|ちめい} (unusual place names)

CULTURAL NOTE: Japanese place names often have historical, topographical, or religious origins. Many come from Ainu language in Hokkaido, or reflect local features (rivers, mountains, temples).
